title: The hint that points back to chat

steps.path: After the initializing screen's button sends you to the terminal
steps.headline: Three shapes for the little hint that points you back to the chat button. Which one looks least out of place?

variants.label: A — Quiet bubble
variants.summary: Built out of the same panel the app's other pop-ups use, with a small arrow aimed at the chat button. Draws the least attention of the three.
variants.measured: 300 px wide, 30 px tall — the same height as the toggle it points at
variants.risk: On the Light theme it is a near-white box sitting on a near-white terminal, and the thin outline is nearly all that separates them.

variants.label: B — Filled bubble
variants.summary: Same shape and arrow, filled with the theme's highlight colour so it stays readable no matter what the terminal is printing behind it.
variants.measured: Same 300 px box; the fill is the only difference from A
variants.risk: That colour is what the app uses to mark the control you are currently on, so a filled bubble reads a bit like a stray second copy of the Terminal button.

variants.label: C — Shelf under the toolbar
variants.summary: Squared off at the top and hung directly off the toolbar's bottom edge, so it reads as part of the window frame rather than a box floating over your terminal. No arrow.
variants.measured: Same width; sits 8 px higher, flush against the toolbar
variants.risk: Nothing points at the chat button any more — the shelf only starts underneath it, which is a weaker hint if your eye is elsewhere.

steps.risk: All three cover the first line or two of terminal output while they are up. The ✕ and switching back to chat both clear them.

steps.headline: The wording is what makes the bubble as wide as it is. How much of it do you want to keep?

options.label: Keep "Click here to switch back to chat view"
options.summary: Your exact words. Nothing to re-decide, and it is the most explicit for someone who has never noticed the toggle.
options.measured: 300 px — about a quarter of the window on a laptop, and it reaches the ✕ on a phone
options.cost: On a phone and on your own touchscreen, "Click" is the wrong verb for what you actually do.

options.label: "Back to chat view"
options.summary: The arrow already does the pointing, so the words only have to name where the button goes.
options.measured: About 150 px — half the width, and it clears the terminal's first line on a phone
options.cost: Says less. Someone who did not follow the arrow has less to go on.

options.label: "Switch back to chat view here"
options.summary: As explicit as your version, minus the verb that only makes sense with a mouse.
options.cost: Still a wide bubble, so it still covers a line of terminal output.
